Multiplier-resampling (MR) estimates table (bootstrap-table format)

Source: R/mr_estimates_table.R
mr_estimates_table.Rd

Renders the selected subgroup's MR de-biased estimate (forestsearch() with mr_inference = TRUE) in the gt layout of the bias-corrected table produced by summarize_bootstrap_results().

Usage

mr_estimates_table(fs, boot_results = NULL, est.scale = "hr", digits = 2)

Arguments

fs

A forestsearch() result with a non-NULL mr_inference element.

boot_results

NULL (default) to build the table from fs alone, or a forestsearch_bootstrap_dofuture() result used as the template for the descriptive columns, the naive effect, the complement row, and the subgroup footnote. A template must contain FSsg_tab and SG_CIs.

est.scale

Character, "hr" or "1/hr"; passed to format_bootstrap_table(). With a template it should match the scale of boot_results; without one, "1/hr" inverts every ratio (limits swap, and a one-sided lower bound becomes an upper bound) and is accepted for ratio measures only.

digits

Integer display precision (default 2), applied with the same reformatter summarize_bootstrap_results() uses so the two tables align.

Value

A gt table. Without a template it carries the attribute "mr_values": a data frame, one row per subgroup (row "H", "Hc"), of the numbers the table displays, on the effect scale of fs$mr_inference (before any "1/hr" inversion): naive_est, naive_lower, naive_upper, debiased_est, ij_lower, ij_upper, and, when present, field_bound and bonferroni_bound (NA where a complement quantity was not computed; the complement's naive columns are then the descriptive table's own robust Cox fit, not stored here).

Details

With a bootstrap template (boot_results supplied): the descriptive columns (sample size, medians/RMST or rates) and the naive effect do not depend on which de-biasing method was used, so they are inherited from a full-bootstrap (FB) result used as a template; the bias-corrected column is replaced with the MR values from fs$mr_inference – the de-biased estimate for the selected subgroup and, when MR was run with include_complement = TRUE, for the complement as well (otherwise the complement cell is marked, since MR de-biases the selected subgroup only).

Without a template (boot_results = NULL, the default): the table is built from fs alone. The descriptive columns are computed from fs$df.est (the analysis data with the declared rule's treat.recommend) by the builder the bootstrap uses (SG_tab_estimates(); for GLM outcomes its GLM counterpart), one row for the selected subgroup and one for its complement in the analysis data. The naive effect is fs$mr_inference$naive (and $complement$naive) with its robust (sandwich) limits, and its header says so. The MR columns follow: the de-biased estimate with its IJ interval (debiased); when fs$mr_inference$field exists, the field one-sided 95% bound (field$lower_1s for the selected subgroup, field$complement$upper_1s for the complement); and when the joint block exists, the Bonferroni pair (field$joint$bonf_lower_H, field$joint$bonf_upper_Hc). The field and Bonferroni columns appear only when those quantities exist. Complement cells carry MR values only when MR was run with include_complement = TRUE (and the complement field with field_complement = TRUE); otherwise they are marked with an em dash, as with a template.

With a template, the selected-subgroup row is matched by its bias-corrected string (boot_results$SG_CIs$H_bc) rather than by position, so the substitution is robust to row ordering. The MR de-biased confidence interval is a leading-order approximation of the full-bootstrap infinitesimal-jackknife interval – it comes from the IJ variance computed on the multiplier draws under ci_method = "ij" or "field" (the forest-search path defaults to "field", which adds the field bounds; the DINA and GRF paths default to "ij"), and from the subgroup robust SE only under ci_method = "wald". Either way the bias-corrected cell may differ slightly from the full bootstrap even when the naive effect matches exactly.

For GLM outcomes the effect columns follow the fit's orientation: the naive and MR values are those of fs$mr_inference, on the scale of the fit's own estimates; the descriptive table's estimator (which gives the complement's naive cell when MR did not cover the complement) is built with the fit's stored adverse_outcome or, when none is stored, with forestsearch()'s rule (TRUE for binary and count outcomes, FALSE otherwise); and a template's effect column comes from forestsearch_bootstrap_dofuture(), which builds its estimator with the same rule. With the default est.scale = "hr", the descriptive columns Rate(C) or Mean(C), Rate(T) or Mean(T), and their raw difference Diff (treated minus control) are the raw outcome and do not follow it. So for an unadjusted fit where a lower outcome is adverse (adverse_outcome = FALSE, the default for continuous outcomes) the effect and Diff have opposite signs: an MD is -Diff, an RD is -Diff / 100, and the log of an OR or RR has the sign opposite to Diff. Count outcomes and the rate measures (IRR, IRD) are not reoriented (see make_effect_estimator()).

See also

forestsearch() for the mr_inference switch and the vocabulary section; fs_mr_inference() for the MR computation itself; forestsearch_bootstrap_dofuture() for the full bootstrap that supplies the template; fs_fdr_report() for harm-confirmation threshold sweeps; summarize_bootstrap_results(), format_bootstrap_table()
